claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ (the Terraform state backend guide) exists.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is an environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service that specifies the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API (for example `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`).
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
In self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN, so a separate domain/second DNS record for the Terraform-compatible API is not required.

In the Terraform state backend guide (/docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/), the domain `tf.pulumi.com` is used in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name, so self-hosted users substitute their PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value in those places.
The `TF_TOKEN_*` environment variable name used for Terraform/OpenTofu authentication is derived from the backend domain, so it must use the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value for self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
The self-hosted Pulumi Cloud Terraform-compatible API is served on the domain configured by PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN, which may differ from the Pulumi API domain PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
